structure: Part 6, Accessibility and security. Read in full: tests/animals/a11y (README.md and 10 specs, 13 tests: journey initial load 1, after input 1, with errors 1, conditional pages 2, dashboard views 3 of which pagination is skipped without a second page, dashboard viewports 1, view states 1, lifecycle states 1, address edit 1, sign-in 1); fixtures/a11y.ts and utils/a11y-utils.ts (the WCAG 2.2 AA standard, axe tags, scan viewports, exclusions mechanism, failure and artefact rules, timeout); tests/animals/security (8 frontend specs, 9 tests: auth, change context, conditional pages, dashboard parameters, documents, draft validation error, lifecycle x2, submitted journey); tests/animals/security/backend/notification-submission.spec.ts (1 test); tests/ins/security/address-book (2 specs, 2 tests: auth and address book lifecycle); fixtures/security.ts (backend API client routed through the ZAP proxy); docs/security.md (ZAP DAST profiles, lanes, scanned and unscanned services, gating). tests/ins/a11y holds only .gitkeep, recorded as a gap. Claims run: a11y standard and suite rules, then each a11y spec's pages and states in spec order, then the security suite's rules from docs/security.md, then each security spec's flow. Security claims are stated in general terms only.

claims.statement: The accessibility suite holds every scanned page to WCAG 2.2 AA, and every a11y describe block is titled with that standard.
claims.quote:
export const WCAG_STANDARD = {
  name: 'WCAG 2.2 AA',

claims.statement: Every scan runs axe with the five WCAG tags needed for AA: wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa, unless a test passes its own tags.
claims.quote: tags: ['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21a', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'],

claims.statement: A passing accessibility scan is not full WCAG 2.2 AA conformance: axe automates only part of the standard, and of the new 2.2 criteria only 2.5.8 Target Size.
claims.quote:
axe only automates part of the standard (only 2.5.8 Target
 * Size among the new 2.2 criteria), so a pass isn't full conformance.

claims.statement: Without the WCAG tags axe would run its default ruleset, which omits the target-size rule, so the tags are what bring target size into the scan.
claims.quote: Without tags axe runs its own default ruleset, which omits target-size

claims.statement: Any accessibility violation on any scanned page fails the test, with one combined error naming each failing page path and each violation's severity, rule id, description, node count, help link and first target.
claims.quote: const header = `Accessibility violations found on ${failed.length} page${failed.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}:\n\n`;

claims.statement: Each scan that finds violations attaches a JSON artefact to the test report, named after the page path.
claims.quote: await testInfo.attach(`accessibility-violations: ${path}`, {

claims.statement: An accessibility test that never runs a scan fails, so every a11y test must scan at least one page.
claims.quote: if (results.length === 0) throw new Error('No accessibility scans were run. Call runA11yScan() at least once.');

claims.statement: Accessibility tests are given a five-minute timeout because they click through several pages and scan each.
claims.quote: const A11Y_SCAN_TIMEOUT_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000;

claims.statement: Each scan waits for the page's DOM to be ready and then, best effort, for the network to go idle, never blocking indefinitely on the second wait.
claims.quote: // Best effort: allow extra settling, but never block indefinitely.

claims.statement: Scans run in axe's non-legacy mode by default, so content inside cross-origin iframes is tested; a scan may opt into legacy mode if axe's window-open hangs, at the cost of not testing cross-origin iframes.
claims.quote:
setLegacyMode() skips that mechanism entirely, at the cost of not
   * testing cross-origin iframes. Set to `true` for scans that hit the hang.

claims.statement: A scan can be narrowed by including or excluding page parts and by disabling named rules; the suite uses only exclusions, each justified as an upstream or not-owned defect.
claims.quote: if (exclude !== undefined) builder = builder.exclude([exclude].flat());
claims.note: No spec in the slice passes include or disableRules; every exclude carries a comment blaming govuk-frontend or the sign-in stub.

claims.statement: Responsive checks re-scan at a narrow portrait viewport of 320 by 568 CSS pixels, the WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow width and govuk-frontend's smallest breakpoint.
claims.quote:
320 CSS px is the WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow width (a 1280px desktop at 400% zoom)
   * and govuk-frontend's smallest breakpoint

claims.statement: Responsive checks also re-scan at a narrow landscape viewport of 568 by 320 CSS pixels, covering WCAG 1.3.4 Orientation and the 256 CSS pixel height threshold of 1.4.10 Reflow.
claims.quote:
a portrait-only scan misses layout that breaks on rotation (WCAG 1.3.4
   * Orientation) and the other half of 1.4.10 Reflow

claims.statement: After a viewport change the suite waits one animation frame before scanning, so viewport listeners and resize handlers have run.
claims.quote: waiting one rAF reliably lets them settle first.

claims.statement: Scans of the origin page exclude the region-of-origin-code radio, because govuk-frontend's conditional-reveal radios set aria-expanded on the input, which axe's aria-allowed-attr rule rejects; the suite treats this as an upstream disagreement, not a service defect.
Scans of the import reason page exclude the reason radios that open a conditional reveal, for the same govuk-frontend aria-expanded reason.
claims.quote: const conditionalReasonRadios = 'input[name="reasonForImport"][aria-controls]';

claims.quote:

claims.quote: Not every reachable state is worth a dedicated scan — weigh the state's value against the test infrastructure it needs.

claims.statement: Security testing is a dynamic scan (DAST) through an OWASP ZAP proxy, with Playwright driving real authenticated journeys through it rather than ZAP crawling.
claims.quote: A DAST (Dynamic Application Security Testing) scan using [OWASP ZAP](https://www.zaproxy.org/) as a proxy. Playwright drives real authenticated journeys through it rather than letting ZAP crawl

claims.statement: Security coverage is traffic-driven: a route no spec drives is invisible to the scan, so the active corpus is curated by hand to drive every route worth attacking.
claims.quote: Coverage is therefore **traffic-driven**: a route no spec drives is invisible to the scan. That is why the `@active` corpus is curated by hand rather than generated.

claims.statement: The passive security profile runs the e2e suite (excluding @active) through ZAP without attacking; the active profile runs only the @active suite and attacks, and is for docker-compose only.
claims.quote:
| `security`        | The e2e suite, excluding `@active` | No — passive only | Cheap, run broadly              |
| `security:active` | The `@active` suite only           | Yes               | Deliberate; docker-compose only |

claims.statement: The active scan is refused on CDP environments, because the @active suite deletes notifications, documents and queue messages and the scan replays them with fuzzed payloads.
claims.quote: **`security:active` is refused on CDP.** The `@active` suite deletes notifications, documents and DLQ messages

claims.statement: The GitHub Action active scan is manual dispatch only, its nightly schedule disabled; its report is published password-protected and reports older than seven days are pruned.

claims.statement: A security run fails if any context's scan hits its 60-minute cap, because a truncated scan reporting no findings is a false clean.
claims.quote: A scan that finishes at the ceiling was cut short, and an incomplete scan reporting no findings is a false clean.

await expect(row).toContainText('Check completed', { timeout: fileUploadTimeouts.virusScanComplete });
